item.title: Ornithologist and Artist Guy Tudor Dies at 91
item.description:
Guy Tudor, a self-taught ornithologist and MacArthur fellow, has died. He was renowned for his precise illustrations of tropical songbirds in definitive field guides.

item.title: Restricted eating hours may reduce cognitive decline in older age
item.description:
A pilot study suggests that limiting meals to a nine-hour window and avoiding food four hours before bed may improve mental skills. Researchers found hints of cognitive improvement in older women who followed these restricted eating patterns.

item.title: Prescribed burns increase giant sequoia survival rates
item.description:
A new analysis shows that giant sequoias in areas treated with prescribed burns are nearly four times more likely to survive extreme wildfires. Researchers suggest controlled fires could prevent thousands of tree deaths across sequoia groves.

item.title: CRISPR enhances immunotherapy effectiveness against prostate cancer
item.description:
Scientists used CRISPR technology to make prostate cancer cells more detectable by the immune system. This experimental treatment significantly improved immunotherapy results in mice and may benefit other hard-to-treat tumors.

item.description:

item.title: Genetic diversity aided brown tree snake invasion in Guam
item.description:
Researchers discovered over 19,000 genetic differences in brown tree snakes using DNA sequencing. This hidden diversity likely helped the population overcome inbreeding and adapt to Guam's environment.

item.title: Ancient one-eyed ancestor shaped vertebrate eye evolution
item.description:
Researchers suggest a tiny, one-eyed organism from 600 million years ago influenced the evolution of all vertebrate eyes. This ancient median eye may still exist today as the human pineal gland.
